newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria to raise gas output by 8.3 million cubic metres.
newsitem.headline: Syria to raise gas output by 8.3 million cubic metres.

text.p: Syria will soon start construction of two major gas projects that would raise output to 18.3 million cubic metres a day at a total cost of $550 million, Oil Minister Mohammed Maher Jamal said on Tuesday.
He told Reuters in an interview that the winner of a tender issued earlier for construction of a $300 million gas project would be announced soon.
He said three companies were competing for the project which includes building a gas plant capable of processing 4.3 million cubic metres per day.

The companies are Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Conoco, and Coastal Corp of the United States. Construction would start soon and the project, near Dayr Azzawr city some 350 km (220 miles) northeast of Damascus, should be completed by 2000, the minister said.
He said studies were in progress for constrction of a second gas project north of the central region to produce four million cubic metres of gas a day.
The project will cost around $250 million and construction should begin this year, the minister said.
He said that Syria's current gas production is around 10 million cubic metres a day, part of which is used to feed electricity generation plants.
"Syria has a very big reserve of gas which ensures a good future for the gas industry in the country," the minister said without giving any figures.
Answering a question on plans for construction of an oil refinery by the private sector in Syria, the minister said the government was still discussing the offer and its feasibility.

Oil industry sources said the Sarakbi group, a private company, had offered to build an oil refinery with a capacity of processing 140,000 barrels a day in accordance with an investment law allowing investors to operate tax-free for the first five years.
There are two oil refineries in Syria now in the cities of Banyas and Homs, each with a capacity of processing 120,000 bpd.
Syria produces around 600,000 bpd of which over 330,000 bpd are exported to the oil market.
